title: Daily Dose #275: Truth in the Inward Being
body:
**"Behold, you delight in truth in the inward being, and you teach me wisdom in the secret heart."**

God is not only concerned with outward behaviour. **PSALM 51:6 (ESV)** says He delights in truth in the inward being. David speaks after his sin has been exposed, and his words remind us that repentance must go deeper than appearance.

It is possible to be sorry about consequences without loving truth inwardly. It is possible to confess enough to reduce pressure while still protecting hidden sin. But God desires truth in the secret heart. He does not heal what we keep covering.

This is mercy, though it may feel painful. The Lord brings truth inward because hidden falsehood destroys. Sin grows in darkness. Pride survives on denial. Healing begins when the heart stops editing itself before God.

**PSALM 32:2 (ESV)** says blessed is the person **"in whose spirit there is no deceit."** That is freedom. Not a life without any sin, but a life no longer hiding behind deception.

Ask God for truth inwardly. Let Him deal with motives, excuses, desires, and secret agreements with sin. He teaches wisdom in the secret heart, and His mercy reaches deeper than the image we present to others.

The secret heart is where many battles are either fed or surrendered. A person may look composed outwardly while inwardly defending resentment, lust, envy, pride, or unbelief. David's prayer refuses that split life. He brings the inward being before God because true repentance does not only want to appear clean; it wants to be made clean. The Lord's mercy reaches the place where the sin was first welcomed.

That is why honesty with God is not something to fear. He already sees, and He is able to cleanse. The hidden place can become the holy place when truth is welcomed and sin is surrendered.
